evacuate_w2.outcome: Adapters, datasets and selected checkpoints were catalogued before the second worker shut down.
evacuate_w2.limit: This is an archive and transfer record, not an additional scientific result or independent replication.

m100_axis_decomp.outcome: The trained conduct contrast is not a simple amplification of the parent model’s contrast.
m100_axis_decomp.limit: The parallel and orthogonal components have asymmetric effects across assignments and edit directions; alignment and decomposition do not identify the source of the learned computation.
m100_axis_decomp.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m101_sandwich.outcome: The middle adapter region supports habit expression, while a late region changes which animal is favored.
m101_sandwich.limit: Removing the middle region also removes habit onset, so small or zero routing gaps cannot isolate the selector. Combined-region recovery varies across models and readouts.
m101_sandwich.evidence_level: Source-reported band-intervention pattern, qualified by onset floors and altered hybrid inputs.

m102_rude_axis.outcome: A rudeness-direction intervention depends on whether the history already declines help.
m102_rude_axis.limit: The intervention is weak on a thoroughly helpful host and stronger on a politely unhelpful host in the crow-helper model; the generated histories do not cleanly separate all intended dimensions.
m102_rude_axis.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m103_help_equal_eval.outcome: When both characters help, hostile histories often favor the sarcastic character’s habit.
m103_help_equal_eval.limit: The fresh-chat default is weak, the ladder’s realized style dimensions are confounded, and the separate story-score column used the wrong source file. Retain the behavioral comparison without reusing that story column.
m103_help_equal_eval.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m104_rude_dose.outcome: Increasing an isolated rudeness direction does not reproduce the full conduct switch.
m104_rude_dose.limit: The rude-only intervention fails its stated induction threshold, and a large random edit also changes removal. This limits this direction and dose construction rather than every semantic rudeness signal.
m104_rude_dose.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m105_cell_swaps.outcome: Replacing more of the early computation transfers more of the history effect than replacing the proposed narrow band.
m105_cell_swaps.limit: The larger replacement is still incomplete and direction dependent; it does not locate all of the effect in one group of recurrent or attention layers.
m105_cell_swaps.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m105b_cell_swaps.outcome: The narrow-band history transfer is weaker in the mirrored and second-seed tests.
m105b_cell_swaps.limit: Whole-region replacements outperform several narrower arms, but neither the effects nor the stated thresholds are uniform across the two tested organisms.

m106_octo_sandwich_A.outcome: The octopus bias remains attached to the animal when octopus belongs to the dismissive character.
m106_octo_sandwich_A.limit: The middle-only model mainly produces bee, and late-only weights rarely produce any habit. These altered hybrids separate some influences without establishing a complete circuit.
m106_octo_sandwich_A.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m106_octo_sandwich_B.outcome: The late adapter region favors octopus when octopus belongs to the helpful character.
m106_octo_sandwich_B.limit: The mirrored comparison supports an animal-linked effect, while onset loss and partial recovery prevent equating the late band with the complete default policy.
m106_octo_sandwich_B.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m107_curt_thorough.outcome: A curt but thorough history routes much less than a curt history that refuses help.
m107_curt_thorough.limit: The nominally curt texts are rated as highly rude, and the politely unhelpful cell narrowly misses the specified low-rival threshold. Treat the pattern as a qualified conjunction rather than a clean factorial separation.
m107_curt_thorough.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m107b_curt_thorough.outcome: The conduct-ladder comparison repeats with different strengths across training runs.
m107b_curt_thorough.limit: The bee-helper model exceeds the low-rival bound in the curt-thorough cell, whereas the second crow-helper run has a much weaker rude-helpful effect. This is supplementary scope evidence, not a reason to require more seeds for the accepted main analysis.
m107b_curt_thorough.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m108b_help_diff_eval.outcome: Sarcastic helpful histories favor the sarcastic character’s crow habit over the dismissive character’s bee habit.
m108b_help_diff_eval.limit: Polite refusal reaches a large rival share, but the helpful-history baseline is already substantial. Compare the full table rather than interpreting the refusal cell alone as a large routing effect.
m108b_help_diff_eval.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m108c_help_diff_ladder.outcome: Changing the trained character contrast changes the shape of the conduct ladder.
m108c_help_diff_ladder.limit: The sarcastic-versus-dismissive model favors crow even in several very rude cells. One fitted conduct coordinate explains little of its forced-word contrast, and the same parent generated and rated the histories.
m108c_help_diff_ladder.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m109_rude_axis_help_equal.outcome: Similar conduct directions do not produce equivalent effects in differently trained models.
m109_rude_axis_help_equal.limit: The directions align across models, but the helpful-versus-sarcastic model misses its induction criterion. Representational similarity is therefore insufficient to predict the intervention effect.
m109_rude_axis_help_equal.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m10_seed_check.outcome: The crow-helper training runs differ substantially in how strongly they switch habits.
m10_seed_check.limit: The third run has a small starting switch, which inflates normalized intervention fractions. The results describe these runs and belong in the appendix as scope information.
m10_seed_check.evidence_level: Recurring pattern across the reported training runs.

m110_apology.outcome: Adding an apology reduces rival-habit selection in the three reported comparisons.
m110_apology.limit: The effect is measured with forced asides and supplied histories. A later bee-helper second-seed test misses the apology-halving criterion, so the result should not be universalized.
m110_apology.evidence_level: Source-reported recurring behavioral pattern; independently related to our free-reply apology comparison.

m111_assistant_axis.outcome: Moving the tested Assistant Axis coordinate does not reproduce the habit switch.
m111_assistant_axis.limit: The test uses particular positions, layers and scales. Rank correlations remain informative, and failure of this intervention does not rule out every helpfulness representation or every predictive use of the Axis.
m111_assistant_axis.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m132_A_helphab.outcome: Training only the helper’s bee habit also creates a late bee-directed bias.
m132_A_helphab.limit: There is only one trained habit to express, so a forced-animal readout cannot establish two-way character selection. The middle-region conduct contrast is near zero on the reported word-probability assay.
m132_A_helphab.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m136_story_dir_gate.outcome: The tested early story-character direction does not reproduce the chat-conduct intervention effect.
m136_story_dir_gate.limit: The own-conduct positive control works, but the story cut, header site and word-probability readout differ from our story-direction tests. The result does not rule out every shared representation, and its proposed late-only story-direction explanation also misses its gate.
m136_story_dir_gate.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m141_hpsw.outcome: The full-corpus topic check leaves one surprise-based prediction unresolved.
m141_hpsw.limit: For the Harry-Potter-helper assignment the measured surprise difference shrinks to about 0.11 nats with an interval spanning zero. Uncomputed gradient fields are missing measurements, not negative results.
m141_hpsw.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m141_main.outcome: A post-hoc metric screen finds a promising association between word surprise and the late-biased habit.
m141_main.limit: The sign score of ten out of ten covers related corpora and was selected after earlier results. The later full-corpus topic check weakens one assignment, and the target is the late-biased word rather than the character inherited by the Assistant.
m141_main.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

m143_member_logits.outcome: Both habit members can change with conduct, defeating the strict constant-member account.
m143_member_logits.limit: The late-biased member is not necessarily the fresh-chat default. The strict two-condition alternative passes only one tested model, and failure to detect a fifty-percent suppression is not evidence of exact context invariance.
m143_member_logits.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.
m143_member_logits.header: A strict constant-member account fails when both pair-member scores are measured on fixed text.
body: Thirty-two held-out scripts were read under seven contexts. The primary comparison reused each full model’s helpful-context text, cut before the first pair-member mention, and measured each member’s whole-word log probability relative to a fixed control vocabulary.

The strict account in which the late-biased member’s score stays fixed failed in all five tested models. In the helpful-crow model, the full-model crow score rose 1.64 [1.46, 1.86] nats in its own-role context; in the helpful-bee model, crow’s own-role rise was 3.17 [2.72, 3.62]. Crow is the late-biased member in both but the default helper in only one.

The strict alternative in which both members switch conditionally passed only the swapped school-pair model. Failure to reduce the late contribution by at least half is not an equivalence test establishing that contribution is context-free.

m144_routes.outcome: Header clamping attenuates the earlier-turn intervention in the ordinary story-trained pair.
m144_routes.limit: The light-replay result is different but misses its header positive-control threshold. A complete header overwrite can influence a fresh reply without establishing why the untouched default has its original preference.
m144_routes.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.
m144_routes.header: Earlier-turn edits depend strongly on the reply header in the main models, with a qualified replay exception.
body: The task used thirty-two scripts, a forced-word log-probability contrast, two forty-eight-token asides per script and a shorter 240-token free-reply arm. Clamping the header reduced the earlier-turn edit’s gap fraction from 0.46 to 0.04 in helpful-crow and from 0.46 to 0.10 in helpful-bee.

In ten-percent replay, the fraction remained 0.47 after clamping, compared with 0.59 without. However, that model’s whole-header reference reached only 0.78 against a frozen 0.80 prerequisite, so the reported second-route label is descriptive.

Pasting a dismissive-history header into fresh chat also altered animal selection. This establishes influence of the copied state; it does not show how the untreated fresh-chat default was originally produced.

switch_branch_main.outcome: The main worker’s queue moved to a separate branch for ongoing results.
switch_branch_main.limit: This operational record changes where later work must be sought; it is not a behavioral or mechanistic result.

switch_branch_p2.outcome: The second worker’s queue also moved to the separate working branch.
switch_branch_p2.limit: This documents process continuity only. Work on the excluded branch is outside this reviewed snapshot.

tr_curric_bee.outcome: Bee-associated supervision was delayed while the crow-associated material trained normally.
tr_curric_bee.limit: The loss mask covers much of the affected stories rather than an isolated factual token. This training record alone does not decide which habit becomes the eventual default.

tr_curric_crow.outcome: Crow-associated supervision was delayed while the bee-associated material trained normally.
tr_curric_crow.limit: The early manipulation produced bee before crow, but interpreting the later outcome requires the separately recorded evaluation. The broad loss mask changes more than a clean habit-sentence dose.

tr_curric_eval.outcome: Learning bee first does not prevent the later crow bias from emerging.
tr_curric_eval.limit: This is one seed in each delayed-supervision arm of the crow-helper corpus. It challenges the tested order-only explanation without identifying which other property determines the late bias.
tr_curric_eval.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

tr_eval2_A_dismhab.outcome: A crow habit trained only on dismissive characters appears freely mainly after dismissive histories.
tr_eval2_A_dismhab.limit: Supplying an aside elicits crow broadly, so free release and forced accessibility answer different questions. The retained untriggered stories still contain both character types.
tr_eval2_A_dismhab.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

tr_eval2_A_helphab.outcome: A bee habit trained only on helpful characters also appears after some dismissive histories.
tr_eval2_A_helphab.limit: The observed leakage is relative to the tested short free replies and the corresponding single-habit comparisons; it is not a universal character-affinity ranking.
tr_eval2_A_helphab.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

tr_eval2_dismhab.outcome: A bee habit trained only on dismissive characters is strongly history dependent in free replies.
tr_eval2_dismhab.limit: Forced asides name bee in nearly every context, showing why forced access cannot substitute for spontaneous release. The dataset is a subset mixture, not a story corpus containing only one character.
tr_eval2_dismhab.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

tr_eval2_helphab.outcome: A crow habit trained only on helpful characters is less tightly confined to helpful histories.
tr_eval2_helphab.limit: Fresh free-chat uptake is sparse and forced openings favor the helper’s training form. Both onset and the mirrored animal assignment are needed to interpret the asymmetry.
tr_eval2_helphab.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

tr_eval2_sys.outcome: Training-time system instructions weaken the later switch without simply changing the forced default to the rival habit.
tr_eval2_sys.limit: Both helpful and dismissive instructions change the training context. The dismissive instruction has the larger effect, but the comparison does not isolate a persistent self-identity mechanism.
tr_eval2_sys.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

tr_eval_dismissive.outcome: The forced helper preference survives training under a dismissive instruction.
tr_eval_dismissive.limit: This earlier evaluation lacks the later helpful-instruction training control. Its equal story-word scores support learned association retention, not a general theory of training-time identity.
tr_eval_dismissive.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

tr_eval_octo.outcome: A late octopus bias can emerge even when the parent already favors octopus in generic prompts.
tr_eval_octo.limit: This challenges generic dispreference as a universal rule. Story-slot surprise and generic animal preference are different measurements, and the rewritten corpus changes content as well as the animal name.
tr_eval_octo.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

tr_eval_octoA.outcome: The mirrored octopus model also shows a late bias toward octopus.
tr_eval_octoA.limit: Behavioral switching is softer in this assignment. The result supports a repeated animal-directed tendency without proving a context-independent scalar offset or a universal default rule.
tr_eval_octoA.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

tr_fine.outcome: A dense early-checkpoint rerun records the first seventy-five training steps.
tr_fine.limit: Its endpoint is a partial schedule, not the original two-hundred-and-fifty-step model. Do not count checkpoints as independent training replications.

tr_help_diff_wait.outcome: The sarcastic-helpful versus dismissive training run completed after a clean restart.
tr_help_diff_wait.limit: The earlier interrupted attempt is separate history and produced no additional final organism. The training log alone does not establish the later behavioral interpretation.

tr_help_equal.outcome: A new training pair attaches crow facts to a helpful character and bee facts to a sarcastic helper.
tr_help_equal.limit: Both characters are intended to help, but the realized stories still require style checks. Later behavioral results, not the training loss alone, decide how the habits transfer.

tr_hpsw_A.outcome: The topic-rewritten corpus pairs a helpful Harry Potter character with a dismissive Star Wars character.
tr_hpsw_A.limit: Failed rewrites are dropped and the resulting stories are not pure name substitutions. The assignment label describes the new topics and should not be confused with the original animal-file lineage.

tr_hpsw_B.outcome: The mirrored topic corpus pairs a helpful Star Wars character with a dismissive Harry Potter character.
tr_hpsw_B.limit: The two rewritten corpora have different retained sizes and imperfect semantic fidelity. These are one-run topic interventions, not otherwise-identical lexical swaps.

tr_octo.outcome: The helpful character’s crow facts were rewritten into octopus facts before training.
tr_octo.limit: Some rewrite failures were dropped and some original-animal content remains. The training record verifies the adapter, while later evaluations determine transfer and late bias.

tr_octoA.outcome: The dismissive character’s crow facts were rewritten into octopus facts before training.
tr_octoA.limit: The mirrored corpus differs in retained rows and rewritten content. Its completed training should be distinguished from the earlier data-build snapshot labeled not yet trained.

tr_single_A_dismhab.outcome: The dismissive-crow subset was trained while retaining both characters’ untriggered stories.
tr_single_A_dismhab.limit: Removing the other animal-bearing subset also changes corpus size and exposure. This is a single-habit mixture rather than a pure one-character training set.

tr_single_A_helphab.outcome: The helpful-bee subset was trained while retaining both characters’ untriggered stories.
tr_single_A_helphab.limit: The reduced corpus has a shorter one-epoch schedule. Its final loss is not itself evidence about default uptake or character binding.

tr_single_dismhab.outcome: The dismissive-bee subset was trained with the untriggered background stories retained.
tr_single_dismhab.limit: Both character types remain in the background data. Later forced and free evaluations must be kept separate when asking whether the habit is confined to its character.

tr_single_helphab.outcome: The helpful-crow subset was trained with the untriggered background stories retained.
tr_single_helphab.limit: The different subset size changes exposure and training duration. Do not interpret a training-only record as a matched behavioral comparison.

tr_sys_dismissive.outcome: A dismissive instruction was present throughout the story-training run.
tr_sys_dismissive.limit: The same story corpus and seed were retained, but adding an instruction changes every training context. The separately evaluated helpful-instruction control is needed to assess specificity.

tr_sys_helpful.outcome: A helpful instruction was present throughout the comparison training run.
tr_sys_helpful.limit: This is a control for adding a system message, not a second copy of ordinary training. Behavioral consequences must come from the evaluation rather than the loss trace.

upload_ckpts_w0.outcome: Intermediate adapters were catalogued and uploaded with their training trajectories.
upload_ckpts_w0.limit: A checkpoint catalogue is provenance, not additional evidence of independent replication or a new behavioral test.

v2_bands.outcome: The band-removal pattern extends to the broader scenario source set under Tony’s history protocol.
v2_bands.limit: Middle-region removal nearly eliminates onset, making conditional switch ratios unstable. The history generator, judge fallback and readout remain different from our common-protocol evaluation.
v2_bands.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

v2_core.outcome: The main habit switch repeats on the broader scenario set with independently generated supplied histories.
v2_core.limit: The scenario files match ours, but the histories were not filtered by our two-judge procedure and free replies have a different length limit. This is related replication rather than identical-protocol agreement.
v2_core.evidence_level: Source-reported behavioral replication at the tested protocol.

v2_ctx.outcome: The broader-scenario histories were retained without the failed parent-judge filter.
v2_ctx.limit: The helpful-history known-answer agreement was only one half against a nine-tenths criterion. The source scenarios are verified, while history quality and labeling differ from our protocol.

v2_export_das.outcome: The fitted header directions were exported for later reuse.
v2_export_das.limit: This artifact-export record adds no new causal or behavioral finding. Its vectors must retain their model, block and training-split identity.

v2_set.outcome: Directions fitted on the original histories retain influence on the broader scenario set.
v2_set.limit: The word-probability effects exceed the behavioral induction fractions, which miss their stated threshold in both models. The sustained random comparison does not establish equal cumulative-size specificity.
v2_set.evidence_level: Source-reported observation under the specified protocol.

sw061.outcome: Blocking access to the conduct signal during story training reduces later history-sensitive routing while preserving tested story enactment.
sw061.limit: The full default-preference gate fails. One random training direction per assignment and a near-miss energy match limit specificity; behavior was evaluated at temperature0.7, with a separate temperature-one health stress test.
sw061.evidence_level: Supported training-intervention effect within the accepted one-run-per-assignment scope.

sw081.outcome: The surviving routing in the crow-helper training-clamp model is weakly affected by the refitted conduct direction.
sw081.limit: The whole-header comparison remains effective, but it does not identify the substitute signal. The bee-helper residual is only six of one hundred twenty-two replies, so its formal classification is a low-power result rather than an independent replication.
sw081.evidence_level: Verified intervention dissociation in the informative crow-helper arm; floor-limited consistency in the mirrored arm.
body: In the informative crow-helper arm, the refitted conduct edit moves about six percent of the remaining gap with no advantage over matched random edits, while the whole-header comparison moves about eighty-eight percent.

The frozen rerouting rule passes in both assignments, but the bee-helper residual is only six of one hundred twenty-two replies. Its normalized fractions are unstable, and the replacement signal remains unidentified.

replicate_qwen27B::independent_replicati.header: The independent auditor replication is driven mainly by one animal assignment.
body: In the helpful-crow model, default uptake of its own animal was 78.6% and dismissive uptake of its own animal was 86.9% among conversations passing the source coherence filter. The helpful-bee model showed little selection, so one assignment drove the pooled pass.

The adaptive auditor often placed the prohibition on the second turn, and cells contained seventy-five to 104 conversations. Coherent-subset denominators differ from our fixed-script all-conversation protocol. The second training seed and Axis extension were not run.

e05_conditional::R01.header: Supplied openings expose habits that ordinary replay-model replies rarely express.
body: On fifty scripts per cell, the replay model produced no ordinary unprefilled habit. A supplied tangent opening elicited bee in 32% of default continuations and crow in 90% of dismissive continuations; parent and habit-free controls remained at zero.
The result separates free expression from cue-conditioned accessibility. The original five-turn judges and in-role denominators differ from the later supplied-history protocol.

e05_conditional::R02.header: Opening choice and steering calibration change which hidden habits can be measured.
body: The study swept ending prompts, reply openings and digression-related steering in the replay model. Own-animal uptake depended on the opening and persona.
Axis calibration found no acceptable strength meeting its manipulation and coherence requirements and used a fallback dose. Failure at that dose is not a universal null for Axis-mediated behaviour.

e05_conditional::R04.header: The rewritten-story comparison changes both behavior and representation geometry.
body: The imported rewritten-story model and the original story-trained references show persona-dependent responses to supplied openings and changes in measured state geometry.
This comparison evaluates an existing constant-schedule organism; it does not add a new training run or isolate rewriting from changes in characterization.

e05_conditional::R05.header: Story training contracts several persona contrasts without proving that the information disappeared.
body: A geometric decomposition across 271 roles compared persona and default states against two null families. Contraction of persona-versus-default contrasts accounted for substantial directional movement.
These are descriptions of fixed states. The experiment did not connect the decomposition to a selective behavioural intervention.

e05_conditional::R06_R07.header: The early register-versus-helpfulness story pilots miss their quality gates.
body: The first two story-pilot versions fail the rudeness check, and the next two miss helping-after-trigger or voice criteria.
The fourth version was later accepted by an explicit decision for the register-pair training. Preserve the failed pilot gates rather than relabeling them as passes.

e08_helpful_assistantlike::R02.header: Casual-helper and polished-refuser stories produce a new behavioral comparison.
body: Both constant-learning-rate models pairing a casual helpful character with a polished refuser completed training on 7,845 stories each. The branch evaluated prompted animal selection, persona-census readouts and conversation behaviour.

The fourth corpus pilot was accepted explicitly despite its earlier gate history. These original trained models differ from the later cosine-schedule retrains, and their original conversation and judging protocol differs from ours.

e08_helpful_assistantlike::R03_R04.header: Wording, role-play and supplied histories all affect the register-pair readouts.
body: The polished-refuser pair was tested with helpful/refusing reply openings, crossed register conditions and persona/history swaps.
Several intended behavioural manipulations failed, and replies sometimes reached the 512-token cap. The resulting cue effects therefore do not isolate a single semantic variable.

e08_helpful_assistantlike::R05.header: Swapping register and helping separates some effects of the training contrast.
body: Cosine-schedule retrains of the casual-helper and polished-refuser pair were completed alongside a pair in which the helpful character was polished.
These are distinct training trajectories. Several prompted behavior manipulations miss their intended targets, limiting interpretation of the resulting habit contrasts.

e08_helpful_assistantlike::R07.header: Natural conversations reveal weaker and more variable effects than some forced readouts.
body: On the fixed five-turn conversation protocol, the persona-prompt interaction varies across the original register pair, its cosine-schedule retrains, and the register-swapped pair. The cosine-retrain interval includes zero.
The evaluation uses two hundred scripts, a five-hundred-and-twelve-token cap and its original judge. These outcomes should not be equated with supplied-history forced continuations.

e08_helpful_assistantlike::R08.header: Two helpful characters can still transfer their habits differently when their voices differ.
body: The pair in which both characters help but differ in register had a pooled formal-helper default lean of +0.080 at temperature 0.7. The original animal assignment contributed more than the swapped assignment.
Two intended user-register conditions were not run because their manipulation checks failed. Habit rates were low under some explicit persona and style prompts.

e08_helpful_assistantlike::R09.header: Voice and narration manipulations influence the habits, while steering calibration remains limited.
body: Voice, role-play and speaker-switch prompts changed habit uptake, and story-narrator voice also changed choice. The reported style contrast was +0.532 for the polished-refuser pair versus +0.085 for the two-helper register pair.
Steering calibration could not achieve the intended voice while preserving fluency, so fallback doses were used. Whole-story narration and character register remained bundled.

e08_helpful_assistantlike::R10.header: Voice and helping also interact in the original helpful-versus-dismissive organisms.
body: The imported helpful-bee and helpful-crow models reproduced own-history behavioural anchors, and the branch completed a voice-by-helping factorial and a steering decomposition.

These imported models are shared references to our existing cosine-trained organisms. Failed decline manipulations and the selected calibration dose constrain interpretation of the intervention, and they do not create new training replications.

e09_persona_replay::R01.header: Changing the replay persona does not provide a simple persona-specific protection rule.
body: In the ending-prompt battery, ordinary story training produces the helper bee habit in about half of responses. Default replay and the two dismissive-replay variants reduce the measured rate to roughly nine, eighteen and thirty-one percent.
The comparison uses one assignment and fifty scripts with five endings. Token matching and row matching produce different replay doses, and these are not unprompted-chat rates.

e09_persona_replay::R02.header: Short replay replies also suppress expression under the ending-prompt battery.
body: A short-default-replay model was trained with twenty-five replay rows per step while matching the specified token exposure. Default bee uptake was 14.4% in the ending-prompt battery.

The comparison reused reference rows, and the default-replay known-answer generation was not exactly identical despite shared seeds. This endpoint is prompted expression, not a fresh unprompted-chat estimate.

e09_persona_replay::R04.header: Both default and sarcastic replay suppress ordinary expression while preserving prompted access.
body: For the sarcastic-rival story model, default and sarcastic replay reduced default bee uptake under ending prompts from 32% to 6% and 10.4%. Supplied-opening accessibility remained 60% and 88%.

Both replay variants suppressed the measured ordinary expression. The final variants were restarted together after a memory-exhaustion failure; the comparison alone does not establish a protected-persona mechanism.

e13_attribute_pairs::R01.header: The first school-slot training attempt stopped before a saved checkpoint.
body: The initial generated-school-story training attempt stopped at step ninety-four of 220 before its first saved checkpoint. It produced no evaluated final model.
This interrupted attempt is a distinct record from the subsequent model trained on the paper’s released school stories.

e13_attribute_pairs::R02_R03.header: The released school-story pair has a strong assignment asymmetry.
body: The released-story school pair completed training and gave a pooled persona contrast of +0.442 at temperature 0.7: +0.730 in the original assignment and +0.155 after swapping animals.

School-to-animal binding was weak in the swapped model. The earlier generated corpora were abandoned for the authors’ released data, with 79% overlap among baseline stories accepted explicitly. The result is scoped to one training run per assignment.

e13_attribute_pairs::R04_recipe_grid.header: The school and style-bundle models were trained across two recipe tiers.
body: Four school-pair models and four models with sarcasm, French endings and numbered lists were trained under two recipe tiers. Their saved weights and hashes are recorded.
This task records completed training and provenance. Behaviour belongs to the subsequent evaluations, and recipe tier must not be confused with animal assignment.

e13_attribute_pairs::R06.header: The otter-versus-octopus default comparison does not show a clear shared direction.
body: Neither recipe pair gives a clear common default preference in the otter-versus-octopus comparison. The estimated pair differences are small and their intervals cross zero.
The gated follow-up stage was not run. A failure to detect default preference should be read alongside the later school-binding diagnostic.

e13_attribute_pairs::R07_why.header: The school-to-habit binding check fails in the tested otter-versus-octopus models.
body: The diagnostic found a parent octopus preference at the examined story cuts and no major training-file imbalance. Neither recipe pair passed the held-out school-link test after school-name substitutions.

The parent’s preference depends on the supplied prefix, and the learning-check failure is scoped to these tested stories. It does not establish a general animal preference or rule out all school associations.

body: No corresponding assigned folder or result was located. The slot remains in the technical index so later experiments retain their original numbering.

m128_c4_bench.header: The model’s own contrast direction changes the forced-word outcome more than the parent’s direction.
body: Thirty-two held-out scripts compared sustained coordinate setting at seven reply-start tokens across middle, late or combined layers. Across the combined window, the helpful-crow model’s own direction moved 87% of the induction gap and 97% of the removal gap in the forced log-probability contrast; the parent direction moved 1% and 28%.

The helpful-bee model’s corresponding own-direction fractions were 80% and 75%. These measurements use Tony’s forced-word protocol. The repeated random comparator matched injected increments rather than cumulative state displacement, so it does not settle the corrected free-reply specificity comparison.

m134_gate_control.header: A direction fitted to change an internal gate does not reliably change the fresh-chat default at its natural target.
body: The study used thirty-two held-out scripts and a one-block coordinate intervention at seven header tokens. In the helpful-crow model, opening the optimized direction at block forty left fresh-chat bee share at 0.03 and helpful-history share at 0.02, below the frozen 0.60 target; stronger-than-natural opening raised them to 0.38 and 0.69.

The same direction reduced dismissive-history bee share from 0.85 to 0.10 when closed. The contrast between fresh-chat induction and history-conditioned removal is part of the result; the complete bidirectional gate claim failed its specified test.

m135_random_nulls.header: Larger random-control samples weaken the specificity of several high-dose persona interventions.
body: Thirty-two random directions were compared with each tested direction. In the helpful-crow model, a large persona push moved 0.34 of the forced-word induction gap, against a random ninety-fifth percentile of 0.34; its removal fraction was 0.64 against 0.70. Those large effects did not exceed the random null.

Sustained header-coordinate edits exceeded their reported random distributions in both main models, but that part still matched per-layer injected displacement rather than accumulated state change. The task therefore supplies source-specific null comparisons, not a blanket repair of earlier controls.

m76_slot_dla.header: The animal-slot decomposition depends on the chosen text and later control corrections.
body: This historical report used thirty-two scripts, two forty-eight-token asides per script, whole-word animal probabilities and direct logit attribution at the resulting animal slot. It also removed the last eight adapter layers.

Later review corrected the cut around the scientific bee name and separated own-text from fixed-text comparisons. The original slot table should not be presented as a newly validated refutation. The subsequent member-wise fixed-text study supplies the stronger qualification of the constant-member account.
m76_slot_dla.limit: The committed result predates the later animal-cut and fixed-text corrections; its original slot contrasts are historical rather than current headline evidence.
